description: Historical Hurricane-Induced US Gulf Coast Petrochemical Infrastructure Disruption Data 2023 is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Kendall Capshaw, Rice University (rice.edu). In this project we provide downtime and resulting excess emissions data on hurricane-induced disruptions to US Gulf Coast petrochemical complexes as well as corresponding storm and facility characteristics. This data can be used in the regional risk and reliability assessment of petrochemical processing infrastructure subject to hurricane hazard-induced disruptions. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 1 top-level file (CSV). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-hh2w-1a93. Keywords: US Gulf Coast petrochemical processing infrastructure, hurricane hazards, oil and gas. Published 2025-01-18. Facility named: University of Texas at Austin. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
